title: 9-Year-Old's Minecraft Videos Cost Dad $100K and His Job
summary: A 9-year-old boy named Mike loves Minecraft. He started a YouTube channel called "Mighty Mike Plays." But his videos weren't getting many views. So his dad, Dave, helped him set up a small ad campaign — just $20. But then Mike went back to YouTube's ad system on his own. He kept buying ads. The total bill? $118,000! The ads worked — Mike's videos jumped from a few hundred views to tens of thousands. But the money came from Dave's corporate credit card. When his bosses found out, Dave lost his job. Now he has about a month to pay back the money, or he might lose his house. Dave posted a video about what happened. It got over 3 million views. Some people feel bad for him. Others are skeptical. A popular YouTuber named MoistCr1tikal thinks it might be a scam. He noticed Dave is selling T-shirts instead of asking for donations. Dave says he's not trying to guilt anyone. "I genuinely have no idea what our lives are going to look like a month from now," he said. This isn't the first time kids have run up huge bills online. Many games and apps make it easy to spend money without parents knowing. Experts say parents should keep an eye on their kids' online accounts.
why_it_matters: It shows how easily real money can be spent online without anyone meaning to, so families should talk about passwords, cards, and who is allowed to click 'buy'.

questions.correct_answer: Keep an eye on their kids' online accounts

background_read: YouTube (a website where people upload and watch videos) pays creators from ads, and anyone can also pay to make their own videos show up more often.

Lots of games, apps and video sites let you spend money with a few taps, and children have accidentally run up huge bills this way — so many countries have rules saying kids under 13 need a parent's permission to have online accounts.
When a bill isn't paid, it usually belongs to the adult whose name and card were used, which is why families are warned to look after their cards and passwords.
Article_Structure: WHO: Mike, a 9-year-old YouTuber, and his dad Dave, who paid the bill with his company credit card.
WHAT: Mike bought $118,000 worth of ads for his channel 'Mighty Mike Plays', and Dave lost his job.
WHERE: On YouTube's ad system, using Dave's corporate credit card.
WHY: Dave has about a month to pay the money back or he might lose his house, and people are arguing about who is really to blame.
